stories.title: Two Australians confirmed dead in Spain’s high-speed train crash
summary: Legal body handling identification says three latest victims include two Australians and a Japanese citizenGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastTwo Australians are among 69 people who died in last week’s high-speed train collision after Spanish authorities confirmed the identities of three more victims.A legal body set up to handle the identification work, made up of police and forensics experts, announced in a statement late on Monday the three latest confirmed victims – two Australians and a Japanese citizen.
They have not been named.

summary: Agriculture, youth visas and emissions agreements nearly tied up under PM’s plan for a much closer relationship with BrusselsThe UK-EU food produce deal: what was agreed and will it affect shoppers?Andy Burnham is preparing to announce billions of pounds of trade deals with the EU covering everything from youth visas to pet passports under his vision of a much closer relationship with the bloc.With the prime minister scheduled to meet his European counterparts in Brussels on 20 November, officials have all but agreed three deals that would allow farmers to sell freely to the continent and travellers to take their animals abroad more easily.

stories.title: Nasa telescope launched in 2004 to plunge back to Earth after failed rescue mission
summary: Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory is expected to re-enter Earth’s atmosphere Wednesday, burning up in the processNasa’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, which has spent two decades studying the most powerful explosions in the cosmos, is expected to re-enter the Earth’s atmosphere on Wednesday, burning up in the process.The satellite, which was designed to operate with its three telescopes for just two years, is no longer able to steer or observe, and its re-entry is uncontrolled.

stories.title: ‘Well-known’ man fails in legal attempt to block Guardian and ITN publishing sexual allegations
summary: Anonymity of individual, whose lawyers had sought injunction citing suicide risk, remains in place subject to any appealA “well-known individual” has failed in his attempt to stop two media organisations from publishing allegations of inappropriate sexual activities towards young women, the high court has ruled.The legal team for the anonymous individual, known in court only as PPT, had claimed he was “highly likely” to attempt suicide if the Guardian and ITN published the allegations, which he denies.

stories.title: Convicted murderer who escaped from Tennessee prison captured in Missouri
summary: Jacob Morley, serving a life sentence for killing a co-worker, slipped through a prison fence last weekA man convicted of murder who escaped from a Tennessee prison was recaptured on Tuesday in Missouri after more than a week on the run, authorities said.Jacob Morley, who was serving a life sentence for killing a co-worker four years ago, was apprehended outside Kansas City, Missouri, before midday by the state highway patrol.

stories.title: Man arrested as girl, 17, found in Oregon after disappearing from Utah last year

summary: Party leader Ed Davey ‘disappointed and upset’ at decision by independent panel after claims original investigation was flawedThe Liberal Democrat peer Chris Rennard has been told there will be no further investigation into sexual harassment allegations made against him, after an independent panel concluded it could not reopen the claim.The party leader, Ed Davey, said he was “disappointed and upset” by the conclusion, having suspended Rennard from the party after an investigation was reopened earlier this year amid claims a previous inquiry was flawed.

stories.title: UK makes huge aid cuts to Commonwealth nations despite warm words at Chogm
summary: Nations in the group fare worse than others, with funding for nature projects especially hard hit even as climate crisis intensifies global needThe UK government has slashed overseas aid to Commonwealth countries, the Guardian can reveal, in contrast to the warm words for the group from King Charles and the prime minister, Andy Burnham, this week.Amid sharp cuts in the UK’s aid budget overall, the Commonwealth has fared poorly, an analysis of the most recent and projected aid figures, seen by the Guardian, has shown.

stories.title: Seven planes across Europe searched or diverted after ‘malicious hoax’ bomb threats
summary: Unclear if series of incidents affecting two UK departures and several Ryanair services, among others, were connectedSeven planes across Europe have been searched or diverted after a series of bomb threats were made to passenger flights, prompting questions as to whether there was any coordination behind the warnings.Two UK departures – one from Heathrow and one from Manchester – were among those threatened in what Downing Street called “malicious hoaxes”, though all planes landed safely and no explosives were found.
